title: Negative Numbers: Add, Subtract, Multiply and Divide

key_sub: For × and ÷, same signs give a positive and different signs give a negative.
body_html:
How it works

Use a number line. Adding a positive number moves right; adding a negative number moves left.

Subtracting a negative is the same as adding: 3 − (−5) = 3 + 5 = 8.

For × and ÷: same signs give a positive, different signs give a negative.

Example

Work out −4 + (−6).

Start at −4 and move 6 to the left.

Answer: −10

Example

Work out −2 − (−7).

Subtracting −7 is adding 7: −2 + 7.

Answer: 5

Example

Work out −6 × 4 and −24 ÷ (−3).

6 × 4 = 24, different signs → −24.

24 ÷ 3 = 8, same signs → 8.

Answer: −24 and 8

Common mistakes

  • Treating 3 − (−5) as 3 − 5. Two minus signs next to each other make a plus.
  • Thinking −4 + (−6) = 10. Adding a negative makes the number smaller.
  • Thinking (−3)² = −9. A negative times a negative is positive, so (−3)² = 9.
  • For a temperature difference, subtracting the wrong way: from −8 °C to 5 °C is 13 degrees, not 3.

faq.q: Why does subtracting a negative number give a bigger answer?
faq.a: Taking away a debt leaves you better off. On the number line, 3 − (−5) means the gap from −5 up to 3, which is 8.

faq.q: What is a negative times a negative?

faq.a: No. (−5)² = 25 because the bracket squares −5. −5² usually means −(5²) = −25.

faq.q: How do I find the difference between −8 °C and 5 °C?
faq.a: Subtract the lower from the higher: 5 − (−8) = 13 degrees.

items.q: In Edinburgh the temperature was 4 °C. It fell by 9 degrees. What is the temperature now?
In Moscow the temperature was −6 °C. It fell by 11 degrees. What is the temperature now?
In Inverness the temperature was −3 °C. It rose by 8 degrees. What is the temperature now?
In Oslo the temperature was −12 °C. It rose by 5 degrees. What is the temperature now?
In Belfast the temperature was 2 °C. It fell by 7 degrees. What is the temperature now?
The temperature was −8 °C at night and 5 °C at midday. How many degrees warmer was it at midday?
items.e: Difference = 5 − (−8) = 5 + 8 = 13 degrees.

items.q: The temperature was −14 °C at dawn and −2 °C in the afternoon. How many degrees warmer was it in the afternoon?
items.e: Difference = −2 − (−14) = −2 + 14 = 12 degrees.

items.q: The temperature was −5 °C at midnight and 11 °C at noon. How many degrees warmer was it at noon?
items.e: Difference = 11 − (−5) = 11 + 5 = 16 degrees.

items.q: The temperature was −21 °C overnight and −9 °C during the day. How many degrees warmer was it during the day?
items.e: Difference = −9 − (−21) = −9 + 21 = 12 degrees.
